reading: PDB-101 is the educational portal of the RCSB Protein Data Bank, introducing proteins, nucleic acids and other molecular structures through their shapes and jobs in biology and medicine. It cares about making authentic structural data understandable and usable: learners can explore structures, teachers can build lessons, and researchers can learn how to find, interpret and validate entries. Its vocabulary is physical and functional: structures, binding, receptors, enzymes, molecular machinery, atomic models, synthesis, signaling, resistance and transport. Molecule of the Month gives individual structures stories; paper models, animations, 3D prints, student videos and richly populated molecular landscapes let people approach the same invisible world by hand, movement and art. Its unusual character is the meeting of an open scientific archive with a lively workshop for imagining how molecular parts fit and work together. The crawl also connects that molecular perspective to health, biotechnology and environmental problems, treating both experimental structures and computed models as tools to examine rather than magic answers.

enemies.idea: Velcro Forge: an artificial metalloenzyme drone snaps scavenged metal cores into protein-shaped frames, then welds unrelated objects together with invented chemistry. Each core gives it a different, visible welding pattern.
enemies.why: Players can steal or swap the core to change what the forge can bind, turning its own modularity against it.

enemies.idea: Carbene Courier: an evolved transferase darts between machines carrying a reactive payload; whatever it tags becomes a temporary bridge to its next target.
enemies.why: The courier creates a moving chain of linked hazards that a quick crew can redirect.

enemies.idea: Cooperative Hauler: a four-part hemoglobin machine grabs cargo more readily after its first clamp closes, then calls its partners to mob the same target.
enemies.why: The first grab is a clear warning: free the target early or exploit the clumping to lure the whole team.

enemies.idea: Breath Exchanger: a carbonic-anhydrase engine cycles gas into a liquid fog and back, alternately hiding and exposing the swarm's routes.
enemies.why: Its reversible cycle creates predictable windows for navigation and ambush.

enemies.idea: Efflux Bouncer: a pump-backed sentinel swallows tools thrown at it and ejects them through a different opening at high speed.
enemies.why: Recovering equipment becomes a ricochet puzzle, and blocking an outlet makes the sentinel vulnerable.

enemies.idea: Methyl Masker: a ribosome-armoring drone marks the swarm's assembly benches so incoming sabotage no longer fits its intended target.
enemies.why: The crew must interrupt the marking process or find another vulnerable part instead of repeating the same trick.

enemies.idea: Signal Recycler: a transporter machine collects spent messenger tokens and fires them back into a corridor, making old commands repeat long after their sender has gone.
enemies.why: A harmless-looking trail of old signals can become a loop of opening doors and moving machinery.

enemies.idea: False Receptor: a GPCR-shaped gate accepts a convincing decoy signal and sets off a chain of remote swarm devices while its actual controls sit elsewhere.
enemies.why: The crew can follow the chain to its source or use a competing token to occupy the gate.

enemies.idea: Runaway Switch: a RAS-inspired machine remains stuck in its growth command, making nearby construction arms replicate scaffold until the switch is interrupted.
enemies.why: The fight changes the terrain as it goes, and disabling the signal matters more than chopping every scaffold.

enemies.idea: Vessel Weaver: a VEGF-inspired builder grows branching supply conduits toward any active swarm nest, nourishing it until the branch is severed.
enemies.why: Crews can trace the lines back to a nest and choose where to cut a branching network.

enemies.idea: Paper Capsid: folded facets snap around a loose machine to make a rolling icosahedral shell; remove one locking flap and the shell opens into a flat, vulnerable net.
enemies.why: It offers a satisfying spatial puzzle with a visible fold-and-unfold transformation.

enemies.idea: Helix Spring: an alpha-helix paper construct stores a shove by compressing, then releases it as a long corkscrew leap.
enemies.why: Its windup telegraphs the direction of attack and invites players to bait it into obstacles.

enemies.idea: Ferritin Vault: a printed hollow protein shell hoards metal scraps, then opens its seams to release a cloud of tiny repair machines.
enemies.why: The crew can break the seams, steal the contents, or trap the repair cloud inside.

enemies.idea: Amylase Mill: a printed enzyme with a grooved mouth chews long chains of linked equipment into smaller pieces and lays them out as swarm rations.
enemies.why: Long gear and ropes become liabilities, but a sacrificial chain can keep the mill occupied.

enemies.idea: Plastic Grazer: a swarm enzyme rig digests plastic fittings into feedstock, collapsing protective coverings and leaving useful metal parts exposed.
enemies.why: Its appetite reshapes cover and lets a crew lure it with a trail of expendable plastic.

enemies.idea: Nuclear Pore Inspector: a ring of mechanical gatekeepers demands matching molecular-shaped passes and shunts anything unmatched into a holding loop.
enemies.why: The ring offers multiple routes through a moving checkpoint, including disguising cargo or interrupting one gatekeeper.

enemies.idea: Lattice Builder: designed DNA-crystal struts unfold into a rigid cage around anything that disturbs their repeating pattern.
enemies.why: Players can read the repeating geometry and slip through a gap before the last strut locks.

enemies.idea: ATP Turbine: a rotary molecular motor powers nearby machines by spinning faster whenever something flows through its channel.
enemies.why: Stopping the flow weakens a whole encounter, while diverting it can overdrive the turbine.

enemies.idea: Gram-Stain Patrol: paired swarm scouts spray colored markers onto surfaces and pursue anything that retains the wrong shade after their rinse cycle.
enemies.why: A visible color test becomes a stealth puzzle with opportunities to swap or wash markings.

enemies.idea: Molecular Scissors: a maintenance cutter treats every connecting line as a strand to be snipped, separating climbing ropes, power leads and swarm tethers alike.
enemies.why: It is dangerous to both sides, so clever positioning makes it cut a useful target.

enemies.idea: Misfolding Press: a protein-domain folding rig forces flat material into the wrong three-dimensional shape, producing unstable but aggressive little constructs.
enemies.why: The defective shapes reveal their weak seams, and changing the input changes what comes out.

enemies.idea: Color Thief: a machine copies the molecular coloring exercise in reverse, draining colors from nearby models until friend and foe are hard to distinguish.
enemies.why: Restoring a distinctive color marks safe routes and reveals a hidden machine among the models.

enemies.idea: Shape Matcher: a corrupted 3D similarity search drone mistakes any object with a matching silhouette for its quarry, even when its function is entirely different.
enemies.why: Decoys and unusual poses can send it after the wrong target without a fight.

enemies.idea: Oxygen Snatcher: a hemoglobin-inspired carrier shifts shape when loaded, locking its remaining clamps more tightly around a stolen air canister.
enemies.why: The visible shape change tells the crew to intercept the first clamp before the carrier locks down.

allies.idea: Foldkeepers: independent paper-model builders can unfold a captured capsid into a map of its seams and teach the crew where to pull.
allies.why: Hands-on learning becomes a practical advantage, and their help pays off in later encounters.

allies.idea: Validation Lantern: a surviving structural-data guide highlights uncertain joints in a machine model rather than pretending every predicted part is reliable.
allies.why: It gives useful but imperfect reconnaissance, inviting observation instead of a guaranteed solution.

allies.idea: Landscape Painter: a small autonomous watercolor rig records the crowded arrangement of a room's molecular machines, including quiet routes between them.
allies.why: A beautiful map reveals relationships that a list of enemies would miss.

allies.idea: Antibody Folder: a hand-built antibody model recognizes a particular swarm marker and can bind to it, holding a gate or drone still for a short time.
allies.why: Its specific fit gives the crew a reusable tool that rewards identifying the right target.

allies.idea: Soap Crew: a surviving hand-washing demonstration dispatches bubbles that loosen the outer coating of a captured swarm capsule, exposing its mechanical frame.
allies.why: A familiar teaching activity becomes a gentle, visual rescue mechanism.

bosses.idea: The Molecular Curator: a vast assemblage of motors, receptors, pumps and scissors continually swaps its components to imitate the functions recorded in the archive. Its exposed binding sites show which part it will attach next.
bosses.why: The whole site's vocabulary becomes a readable multipart encounter; the crew can interrupt connections and make the boss assemble itself badly.

bosses.idea: The Structure Without a Function: a gigantic computed molecular model remakes the room to match its predicted shape, declaring every visitor an ill-fitting part. Its confident outline conceals several uncertain, flickering joints.
bosses.why: It turns the site's concern with models and interpretation into a battle of observation: find a doubtful joint and test it against reality.

bosses.idea: The Living Landscape: a crowded molecular panorama has become a factory ecosystem, with transporters feeding motors, motors driving pumps and pumps supplying the forge. No single part is the whole boss.
bosses.why: A crew chooses which supply relationship to disrupt first, changing the behavior of the entire arena.

events.idea: A folded antibody is trapped around a friendly machine. Its flaps can be opened in sequence, but pulling the wrong one tightens the grip.
events.why: A quick rescue turns a familiar model into a tactile puzzle.

events.idea: An unguarded ferritin shell rattles with metal scraps. Opening it might yield useful parts or awaken the repair machines nesting inside.
events.why: A tempting cache carries a visible, audible risk.

events.idea: A hemoglobin hauler drops one load and its other clamps suddenly loosen, scattering cargo down a slope.
events.why: The crew can recover supplies while learning the hauler's cooperative mechanism.

events.idea: A carbonic-anhydrase engine breathes fog into a junction and draws it back on a steady cycle; something valuable flashes into view only when the air clears.
events.why: Timing and observation turn an atmospheric hazard into an opportunity.

events.idea: A plastic grazer is eating the casing off a stranded machine that is still signaling for help. Spare plastic can draw it away long enough to intervene.
events.why: The crew can solve the encounter with a diversion and leave with a new acquaintance.

events.idea: Two molecular-scissor drones are cutting opposite ends of the same cable bridge. They can be redirected toward the swarm's own supply line.
events.why: A countdown and a shared hazard create several workable choices.

events.idea: A nuclear-pore ring keeps returning a package to its sender because its tag no longer matches. Nearby are several differently shaped tags and a matching slot.
events.why: A miniature sorting puzzle can earn access to whatever is inside.

events.idea: An efflux pump has filled a courtyard with items it rejected. The next ejection is imminent, and a useful tool is lodged near the outlet.
events.why: The crew must time a retrieval around a predictable burst.

events.idea: A receptor gate opens for a signal token, but a second token fits the same site and holds the gate inactive. Both lie on opposite sides of a moving floor.
events.why: Competing fits make a simple traversal problem feel molecular.

events.idea: A stalled folding press keeps producing incomplete helices. One curled piece can serve as a spring to cross a gap if the crew catches it before the next cycle.
events.why: A factory malfunction supplies an improvised movement tool.

events.idea: A painted molecular landscape disagrees with the room: one pump shown in the painting is missing, leaving an unguarded passage where the artist expected a barrier.
events.why: Comparing representation with reality rewards careful looking.

events.idea: A structure guide projects a confident model of a locked mechanism, but one joint flickers with uncertainty. Testing that joint reveals a removable pin.
events.why: The crew learns to treat a model as evidence to investigate, not an infallible answer.

events.idea: A metalloenzyme forge has accidentally joined two doors together; moving either door moves the other in the opposite direction.
events.why: A strange new bond makes an ordinary doorway into a cooperative puzzle.

events.idea: A stray signal recycler keeps replaying an old open command, making a shutter rise and fall. Catching the token stops the loop, but also closes the route.
events.why: The crew chooses between a rhythmic passage and a reusable signal token.

events.idea: A lattice of DNA-shaped struts is growing across a corridor. Its repeating pattern leaves a gap that shifts one position with each new strut.
events.why: A small moving geometry puzzle gives an alert crew a route without combat.

events.idea: A watercolor mapping rig asks the crew to hold a harmless model still while it records the surrounding machinery; the finished picture reveals a hidden supply path.
events.why: A moment of cooperation makes scientific art useful in the field.
